title: Hruday centre-symmetry transfer across gauge groups with recorded obstructions
accepted: Under the frozen BD1 convention (per-link electric term 8 C_2 with C_F=(N^2-1)/(2N) for SU(N), C_2(n)=n^2 for U(1), C_2(l)=l(l+1) for SO(3) and C_2=1 on the odd Z2 state; face energy 32 C_F; magnetic term -(tau/3) W with W = Re chi_fund/dim fund; creation sign psi=e^{-C} Omega_0 and omega(W) = -2 Re (W Omega_0, c^(1)) + O(tau^2)), on the one-plaquette finite graphs H_FG(G) (|tau| below 48 C_F) and on the group-G whole-star box models H^G_N on the open centered boxes Lambda_N, N at least 2, each box separately for |tau| below its Kato radius 12 C_F/(21(2N)^3), for G in {SU(2), SU(3), SU(4), SU(5), U(1), Z2, SO(3)}: the Haar moments E[W^k], k=1..4, and the first-order coefficients of omega(W)/tau (1/144, 1/1152, 1/2880, 1/5760, 1/96, 1/48 and 1/864 in that order) agree exactly between the characters route (forward) and Weyl integration on the SU(N) torus (reverse); the link-flip lemma holds on these models for SU(2), SU(4), U(1) and Z2, whose central elements -I, -I, e^{i pi} and the nontrivial element act as -1 on the Wilson representation, with E_3 verified on Lambda_2, Lambda_3, Lambda_4 and the 24-link coarse factors and E_2 on [-N,N]^2 by exact enumeration; the first-order parity theorem holds for SU(2), SU(4), SU(5), U(1) and Z2 (E[W^3]=0); SU(3) is an obstruction with E[W^3]=1/108, d omega(W^2)/dtau=1/6912 and second-order coefficient 1/589824, SO(3) with 1/27, 1/2592 and 1/331776, and SU(5) a flip obstruction with fourth-order coefficient 1/63403380965376=1/(2^30 3^10) on H_FG(SU(5)); for SU(2) in the AM2/AQ1 zero-selected patterned family at kappa=0, |tau| at most 10^-8 and both signs, omega(W_C)(-tau)=(-1)^{A(C)} omega(W_C)(tau) in every open centered whole-star box and every on-site cutoff, and pointwise for the limit of the named constructions through the BB2 whole-sequence bound at each sign (c'_site=2/984375, q=1/64). Under the frozen convention, the link-flip lemma transfers exactly to the listed gauge groups that have a central element acting as -1 on the Wilson representation and the first-order parity theorem exactly to those with vanishing third Haar moment of W, each with its own first-order Wilson coefficient, on one-plaquette models and on group box models in each box separately; SU(3) and SO(3) are recorded obstructions with exact nonzero coefficients, and SU(5) is a recorded flip obstruction with an exact nonzero fourth-order coefficient; for SU(2) in the zero-selected family at kappa=0 the Wilson-loop mean is odd or even in tau according to the parity of the number of plaquettes of any spanning surface of the loop, in every open centered whole-star box and for the limit of the named constructions; these are statements about named models and one-plaquette finite graphs, not AM2 or continuum statements for other groups, not statements for periodic boxes with an odd side, not uniqueness of any ground state, and not a statement uniform in the lattice spacing a.
limitations: Scope: statements about named finite models only, H_FG(G) (finite graphs; model_is_finite_graph true, transfers_to_aq false) and H^G_N box by box inside a Kato radius that shrinks like N^-3; nothing is claimed for all N at once for any group other than SU(2), no limit state is constructed for any other group, and no AM2, AV1, AQ, BB1 or BB2 statement and no dictionary to a bare coupling is transferred to SU(3), SU(4), SU(5), U(1), Z2 or SO(3); each is recorded as an obligation.

The group-cell oddness statements use simplicity of the finite-box ground eigenvalue from Kato's theorem with a sufficient, not sharp, radius (12 C_F/F_N with F_N=21(2N)^3 retained faces; 48 C_F on one plaquette); this is simplicity in a finite box, not uniqueness of any ground state, and the word "unique" in contract items 1 and 6 is read that way.

No flip or parity statement is made on any periodic box with an odd side. The recorded obstruction is that E_3 and E_2 meet seam plaquettes evenly when the keyed coordinate has an odd side (16 on 3x4x4, 4x3x4 and 4x4x3; 24 on 3x3x4; 4 on the 4x3 torus); E_2 still meets every plaquette of the 3x4 torus once, and by GF(2) elimination some flip set exists whenever every coordinate plane has an even plaquette count (at most one odd side); these are recorded findings, not claims.

The SU(2) corollary inherits the AW1 flip lemma, AM2 simplicity and cutoff removal and the BB2 whole-sequence convergence with their own limitations (the named constructions F1 and F2 only; no statement about other states or boundary conditions); it is made at kappa=0 only, not at a nonzero selected triple and not for F2 or literal vertex boxes; the loop and surface enumerations audit the identity |C cap E_3| = A(C) mod 2 and do not replace the proof.

Exact rational arithmetic decides every value; decimals are truncated previews (the reverse report prints 1.57720727258e-14 for omega_4 of SU(5), a text slip; the exact value 1/63403380965376 and the results preview 1.57720295790e-14 stand). Kato's theorem, Peter-Weyl, the Weyl integration and character formulas, Schur-Weyl duality and Schur's lemma are cited, not machine-checked; the finite enumerations and fixtures audit their finite consequences.

model: One-plaquette finite models H_FG(G) = 32 C_2 - (tau/3) W on class functions of the plaquette holonomy and group-G whole-star box models H^G_N for G in {SU(2), SU(3), SU(4), SU(5), U(1), Z2, SO(3)} under the frozen convention (per-link 8 C_2 with C_F=(N^2-1)/(2N) for SU(N), n^2 for U(1), C_2(odd)=1 for Z2, l(l+1) for SO(3); magnetic -(tau/3) sum W_f with W_f=Re chi_fund(U_f)/dim; face energy 32 C_F); Haar moments; the flip sets E_3 on Z^3 boxes and coarse factors and E_2 on Z^2 boxes; the SU(2) zero-selected family (AM2/AQ1, |tau|<=10^-8, kappa=0) in open centered whole-star boxes and the limit of the named constructions (BB2)
decision: Admit the centre-symmetry transfer ledger, paired with exact agreement of the characters route (forward) and the Weyl-integration route (reverse) and of the skeptic's three routes on 141 cells. Haar moments E[W^k], k=1..4: SU(2) 0,1/4,0,1/8; SU(3) 0,1/18,1/108,1/108; SU(4) 0,1/32,0,7/2048; SU(5) 0,1/50,0,3/2500; U(1) 0,1/2,0,3/8; Z2 0,1,0,1; SO(3) 0,1/9,1/27,1/27. First-order Wilson coefficients of omega(W)/tau under the frozen convention (tier exact_first_order): SU(2) 1/144 (the admitted value, reproduced as a convention check only), SU(3) 1/1152, SU(4) 1/2880, SU(5) 1/5760, U(1) 1/96, Z2 1/48, SO(3) 1/864; the same on the box models. Criterion A (flip): a central element acting as -1 on the Wilson representation gives U_E H(tau) U_E^* = H(-tau); the flip lemma transfers to SU(2), SU(4), U(1) and Z2. Criterion B (parity): E_Haar[W^3]=0 with single-occurrence orthogonality gives vanishing first-order tau-derivatives of omega(W^2) and of the centred correlations; parity transfers to SU(2), SU(4), SU(5), U(1) and Z2. Recorded obstructions with exact nonzero coefficients on the one-plaquette models: SU(3) (no central -1; E[W^3]=1/108; d omega(W^2)/d tau = 1/6912; second-order coefficient of omega(W) = 1/589824), SO(3) (trivial centre; E[W^3]=1/27; 1/2592; 1/331776), and SU(5), which keeps parity but not the flip (fourth-order coefficient of omega(W) = 1/63403380965376 = 1/(2^30 3^10), three routes). Flip sets: E_3 meets every plaquette of the named Z^3 boxes and every face meeting a coarse factor an odd number of times (N=2: 2335 plaquettes, 1082 once, 1253 three times, 1344 retained faces), E_2 meets every plaquette of [-N,N]^2 exactly once. SU(2) area parity: omega(W_C)(-tau) = (-1)^{A(C)} omega(W_C)(tau) in every open centered whole-star box at kappa=0, and pointwise for the limit of the named constructions through BB2 whole-sequence convergence at each sign. Recorded non-blocking: the contract's tier rule and its control disagree on higher-order coefficients (the control governs; both producers label only first-order values with a tier); the forward exports the frozen flip-scope description and names the groups in a separate field, the reverse adds two fields outside the contract list; on periodic tori a flip set exists exactly when at most one side is odd (GF(2) check), so the contract's seam wording concerns E_3/E_2 only and periodic boxes with an odd side stay a scope exclusion; the reverse report prints one omega_4 preview with a wrong decimal (its results carry the exact value); four silent edits caught only by the skeptic's validator; both reports written through the shell after a tool refusal; commit order reverse a1010a4 and forward 5a792b0 before the skeptic package bf1f531, with the skeptic's values final earlier. These are statements about named models and one-plaquette finite graphs: no AM2, AV1 or AQ statement and no dictionary for any group other than SU(2), not uniqueness of any ground state, not weak coupling or continuum and not uniform in the lattice spacing a.
